toc.title: Change Management for Models, Prompts and Data

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MCP: Model Context Protocol; DPA: data processing addendum; BAA: business associate agreement; SLO: service level objective; AI: artificial intelligence

  • What to document for a Claude solution
  • How to give implementation guidance to a delivery team
  • The lifecycle phases and the architect's role in each
  • Change management for models, prompts and data

2Documenting an Architecture

Running case

Lumen Advisory Hands Over a Claims Assistant to the Insurer's Team

  • Lumen's engagement ends in three months; the insurer's team must run, monitor and evolve the system
  • Two prior projects failed to survive hand-off because prompts lived in a developer's notebook

Document Contents
Context and goals Problem, users, success criteria, constraints, non-goals
Architecture overview Components, pattern, data flow, trust boundaries, platform and region
Decision records (ADRs) Decision, options, trade-offs, date, owner, status
Interfaces API and tool schemas, MCP servers, authentication, error handling
Prompts and configuration Versioned system prompts, templates, model IDs and parameters, retrieval settings, Skills, CLAUDE.md
Data Sources, ownership, chunking and index design, refresh schedule, retention, access rules
Evaluation Datasets, metrics, thresholds, how to run the eval suite, results history
Security and compliance Threat model, controls, regime mapping, DPAs and BAAs, audit evidence
Operations Dashboards, alerts, SLOs, runbooks, incident process, on-call, cost budgets
Handoff Known issues, backlog, upgrade path, contacts
  • Docs live with the code: in the repository, reviewed with changes; keep prompts, schemas and evals in version control.
  • Use diagrams (context, components, sequence for key flows, data flow) and keep them current.
  • Write for the reader's task: onboarding, changing a prompt, responding to an alert.
  • Do not store secrets in docs; point to the secrets manager.
Exam tip

A complete handoff includes versioned prompts and configuration, evals, runbooks and decision records, not only code and a diagram.

3Implementation Guidance

  • Give delivery teams clear guidelines: patterns to use and to avoid, prompt and tool conventions, error-handling and retry policy, logging standards, security rules, evaluation gates, naming and versioning.
  • Provide a reference implementation or template repository.
  • Define a definition of done: eval thresholds met, security review complete, runbook written, monitoring in place.
  • Set up reviews: architecture review for significant changes; prompt and eval review for behavior changes.
  • Start thin: a vertical slice (one workflow end to end with eval and monitoring) before widening.
  • Capture coding-assistant conventions for the team (CLAUDE.md, shared settings, Skills) so AI-assisted development follows standards (Module 17).

4Lifecycle Phases

Phase Architect's focus Outputs
Discovery Requirements, constraints, data, risk, success criteria Problem statement, risks, baselines (Modules 1 and 15)
Design Pattern, model, retrieval, integration, security, compliance, evaluation plan Architecture, ADRs, threat model
Build and test Prototype, vertical slice, evals, security tests, load tests Working system, eval results
Handoff and launch Documentation, training, runbooks, staged rollout, SLAs Handoff pack, canary plan
Monitor and iterate Dashboards, quality sampling, feedback loop, cost control, change management Improvement backlog, reports
Retire or migrate Model and platform retirements, data deletion Migration plan

5Change Management for Models, Prompts and Data

Change Risk Practice
Model version upgrade or retirement Behavior and prompts shift; old models retire (Anthropic-operated platforms commit to dates; partner platforms set their own) [Dates] Pin IDs; track retirement dates; run regression evals on the new model; migrate by canary; update prompts per the model's guidance
Prompt changes Silent quality shifts Version, review, A/B test, roll back
Data and index refresh Stale or broken retrieval Validate after each refresh; monitor index age
Tool or API changes Breaking schemas Contract tests; versioned tools; deprecation notices
Regulatory change New obligations Compliance review calendar
Scale growth Rate limits, cost Capacity plan, tiers, batch, caching
  • Keep an upgrade playbook: evaluate, adjust, canary, monitor, retire the old path.
  • Own the backlog: tech debt in prompts, evals and docs is real debt.
  • Plan knowledge transfer: who owns prompts, knowledge bases, evals and on-call after the architect leaves.
Exam tip

Prompts, schemas and evals are code: version them and review them with the change.

Exam tip

Plan model retirements early: pin, run regression evals, canary, then retire the old path.

6Exam Q&A

S1The architect's engagement ends soon. Which handoff package best lets the client's team operate the system?

  • AA recorded demo of the system working
  • BThe architect's personal notes
  • CVersioned prompts and configuration, the eval suite, runbooks, decision records and architecture and data-flow diagrams
  • DThe source code and a short slide deck
Show the answer

Answer: C. Operations need prompts, evals, runbooks and reasoning, not just code.

S2A prompt change shipped last month cannot be traced. What practice would have prevented this?

  • ALetting each developer keep a local copy
  • BDocumenting prompts only in a presentation that is shared with the sponsor at the end of each project phase
  • CStoring prompts in a shared chat thread
  • DKeeping prompts, templates and parameters in version control with review, tests and release notes
Show the answer

Answer: D. Prompts are code, so keeping them in version control with review, tests and release notes makes every change traceable.

S3A model used in production will be retired on a published date. What is the best approach?

  • AIgnore the date because aliases update themselves
  • BSwitch all traffic immediately without testing
  • CTrack the date, run regression evals on a replacement, canary the migration and update prompts as needed
  • DWait until the model stops working and then switch
Show the answer

Answer: C. Plan migrations early with evals and a gradual rollout.

S4Which TWO belong in a definition of done for a new Claude feature? Select TWO.

  • AEval thresholds met on the defined dataset
  • BA runbook and monitoring in place
  • CZero open questions about the roadmap
  • DA demo that worked once
  • EThe developer's confidence
Show the answer

Answer: A, B. Quality gates and operational readiness make a feature done.

S5What is the best way to begin building a large Claude solution?

  • ABuild only the user interface first
  • BBuild every component fully before testing any
  • CA thin vertical slice with evaluation and monitoring end to end, then widen
  • DStart with the most complex edge case and build the full architecture around that single scenario
Show the answer

Answer: C. A slice proves the architecture and exposes risk early.

S6Where should architecture documents and prompts be stored?

  • AIn individual email attachments that each engineer keeps in their own mailbox between releases
  • BIn the production database
  • CIn a wiki that nobody updates
  • DWith the code in version control, reviewed alongside changes, with no secrets
Show the answer

Answer: D. Docs and prompts evolve with the system and need review.

S7Which lifecycle phase includes quality sampling, dashboards and the improvement backlog?

  • ADesign
  • BDiscovery
  • CRetire
  • DMonitor and iterate
Show the answer

Answer: D. Monitor and iterate is the ongoing operation phase, where quality sampling and dashboards feed the improvement backlog.

S8A tool provider changes a response schema and the agent breaks. Which practice reduces such breakage?

  • AContract tests and versioned tool schemas with deprecation notices
  • BRemoving validation from the agent
  • CHard-coding the schema in the prompt only, so that the model adapts when the provider changes it
  • DAvoiding all external tools
Show the answer

Answer: A. Contract tests and versioned tool schemas with deprecation notices catch breaking changes before they reach production.

S9Who should own prompts, knowledge bases and evals after the architect leaves?

  • ANamed owners in the client's team, with documented responsibilities and an on-call or support path
  • BThe model provider
  • CWhoever notices a problem first
  • DNo one specifically; the system is automatic and the model provider will fix any problem that appears
Show the answer

Answer: A. Ownership and knowledge transfer keep the system healthy.

S10Which document records why a vector database was chosen over keyword search alone?

  • AThe deployment script
  • BAn architecture decision record with options, trade-offs and status
  • CThe marketing brief
  • DThe monitoring dashboard that shows which retrieval method was used for each request in production
Show the answer

Answer: B. An architecture decision record documents the options considered and the trade-offs behind a choice such as a vector database.

7Quick Reference Card
